def update_views(self, transform_key=None, show_preprocessed=False, show_images=True,
                 progress_factory=None):
    if transform_key is None:
        transform_key = self.get_best_transform_key()

    is_3d = (self.reg.sources[0].get_size().get('z', 0) > 1)
    is_multi_z_shapes = (len(set(position.get('z', 0) for position in self.reg.positions)) > 1)
    force_2d = is_multi_z_shapes and not is_3d

    # shapes drawn from the same geometry, pairs and qualities are kept, only the image under them replaced
    shapes = None
    build_shapes = self._current_shape_layer(self.viewer, transform_key, force_2d) is None
    # steps weighted by cost: building the view data dominates, and reports from the inside
    view_data_weight = 12
    phases = (self.shapes_weight if build_shapes else 0) + 2 + (view_data_weight + 1 if show_images else 0)

    with self._operation_progress('Refreshing view', progress_factory, phases=phases) as factory:
        if build_shapes:
            with Timer('update_views: create shapes', verbose=self._timing_verbose()):
                # pure geometry, so off the Qt thread to keep the window responsive
                shapes = self._run_off_thread(
                    lambda worker_factory: self._create_napari_shapes(
                        transform_key, force_2d=force_2d, progress_factory=worker_factory,
                        weight=self.shapes_weight),
                    factory)

        # each section built only when viewed: image data as soon as the shapes
        with Timer('update_views: lazy overview', verbose=self._timing_verbose()):
            data = self._run_off_thread(
                lambda worker_factory: self._create_lazy_overview(transform_key,
                                                                  show_preprocessed=show_preprocessed), factory)
        # otherwise (a rotation, or sources it cannot overlay) the fused preview
        if data is None and show_images:
            with Timer('update_views: create fused data', verbose=self._timing_verbose()):
                # fused off the Qt thread; adding it to the viewer below must stay on it
                data = self._run_off_thread(
                    lambda worker_factory: self._create_napari_data(
                        transform_key, show_preprocessed=show_preprocessed,
                        progress_factory=worker_factory, weight=view_data_weight),
                    factory)
        # replaced only once the new data is ready: an empty viewer's welcome screen hides the activity dialog
        with factory(total=1) as pbar, \
             Timer('update_views: add fused data to viewer', verbose=self._timing_verbose()):
            # an overview, not the fusion preview: a naive contrast guess is enough
            self._show_view_image(self.viewer, data, f'{self.reg.fileset_label} data', cheap=True,
                                  keep_shapes=not build_shapes)
            pbar.update(1)

        with Timer('update_views: add shapes to viewers', verbose=self._timing_verbose()):
            self._refresh_view_shapes(transform_key, shapes, progress_factory=factory)
    self.view_mode = ViewMode.OVERVIEW

def update_widgets(self):
    # a dropdown filled later (channels, preview images) is empty until then: only fixed ones map old values
    fixed_choices = {f'{section_id}.{item["name"]}' for section_id, items in self.template.items()
                     for item in items if item.get('options')}
    for param_name, param_widget in self.param_widgets.items():
        # path widgets are set by update_input_output_path(), relative to the project directory
        if param_name not in ('input_output.input_path', 'input_output.output_path'):
            keys = param_name.split('.')
            value = self.params.get(keys[0], {}).get(keys[1])
            if value is not None and param_name in fixed_choices and isinstance(param_widget.widget, ComboBox) \
                    and value not in param_widget.widget.choices:
                value = self._listed_choice(param_name, value, param_widget.widget)
            if value is not None:
                param_widget.set_value(value)
                if param_name == 'input_output.channels_table':
                    # set_value() blocks the table's signals, so channels_table() never sees the loaded value
                    if value:
                        self.set_channels(value)
                    # a loaded project skips update_output_channels(), so attach the color pickers here
                    self.populate_channels_table_color_pickers()
    # a loaded method equal to the widget's default changes nothing, so change_param() does not see it
    self.update_method_params_enabled()

class QColorSwatchButton(QPushButton):
    """A small flat button showing a single color; clicking it opens QColorDialog."""

    colorChanged = Signal(QColor)

    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self._color = QColor()
        self.setFlat(True)
        self.clicked.connect(self._pick_color)
        self._update_style()

    def color(self):
        return self._color

    def setColor(self, color):
        color = QColor(color)
        if color != self._color:
            self._color = color
            self._update_style()
            self.colorChanged.emit(self._color)

    def _update_style(self):
        r, g, b = round(self._color.redF(), 3), round(self._color.greenF(), 3), round(self._color.blueF(), 3)
        self.setText(f'{r}, {g}, {b}')
        text_color = 'black' if self._color.lightnessF() > 0.5 else 'white'
        self.setStyleSheet(
            f'background-color: {self._color.name()}; color: {text_color}; border: 1px solid gray;')

    def _pick_color(self):
        # parented on the window, so the dialog does not inherit this button's background stylesheet
        dialog = QColorDialog(self._color, self.window())
        if dialog.exec():
            color = dialog.currentColor()
            if color.isValid():
                self.setColor(color)

class ArrayTableModel(QAbstractTableModel):
    """Rows of values with row and column labels, read-only: text and colour made only for the cells shown."""

    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.rows, self.row_labels, self.column_labels = [], [], []
        self.background = None
        self._backgrounds = {}

    def set_rows(self, rows, row_labels, column_labels):
        self.beginResetModel()
        self.rows, self.row_labels, self.column_labels = list(rows), list(row_labels), list(column_labels)
        self._backgrounds = {}
        self.endResetModel()

    def rowCount(self, parent=QModelIndex()):
        return 0 if parent.isValid() else len(self.rows)

    def columnCount(self, parent=QModelIndex()):
        return 0 if parent.isValid() else len(self.column_labels)

    def data(self, index, role=Qt.DisplayRole):
        if not index.isValid():
            return None
        value = self.rows[index.row()][index.column()]
        if role == Qt.DisplayRole:
            return '' if value is None else str(value)
        if role == Qt.BackgroundRole and self.background is not None and value is not None:
            key = (index.row(), index.column())
            if key not in self._backgrounds:
                self._backgrounds[key] = self.background(value)
            return self._backgrounds[key]
        return None

    def headerData(self, section, orientation, role=Qt.DisplayRole):
        if role != Qt.DisplayRole:
            return None
        labels = self.column_labels if orientation == Qt.Horizontal else self.row_labels
        return str(labels[section]) if section < len(labels) else None

class QModelTableView(QTableView):
    """A table view over ArrayTableModel, with the QTableWidget calls the plugin uses."""

    valueChanged = Signal(object)
    itemSelectionChanged = Signal()

    def __init__(self, parent=None):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.table_model = ArrayTableModel(self)
        self.setModel(self.table_model)
        # a bound method, not a lambda holding the view: Qt keeps a lambda alive, and through it everything connected
        self.selectionModel().selectionChanged.connect(self._selection_changed)

    def _selection_changed(self, *_):
        self.itemSelectionChanged.emit()

    def value(self):
        model = self.table_model
        return {'data': model.rows, 'index': model.row_labels, 'columns': model.column_labels}

    def setValue(self, value):
        # (rows, row labels, column labels), or magicgui Table's {'data', 'index', 'columns'}
        if isinstance(value, dict):
            value = (value.get('data', []), value.get('index', []), value.get('columns', []))
        rows, row_labels, column_labels = value if value else ([], [], [])
        self.table_model.set_rows(rows, row_labels, column_labels)
        self.valueChanged.emit(self.value())

    def set_background(self, background):
        """`background(value)` gives a cell's QColor, asked only for the cells shown."""
        self.table_model.background = background
        self.table_model._backgrounds = {}

    def currentRow(self):
        return self.currentIndex().row()

    def row_label(self, row):
        labels = self.table_model.row_labels
        return labels[row] if 0 <= row < len(labels) else None

        self._pbar = self.progress_class(
            total=total,
            desc=self.desc,
            **self.progress_kwargs,
        )

        self._started = True

phases is the number of phase-sized units the operation expects and sizes the slices; extra phases take from what is left, missing ones are filled in at the end. A phase worth several siblings claims weight=n units. The bar is painted when the operation starts, before its first phase reports.

class NapariPhaseProgress:
    """One napari progress bar, filling once, for a whole user-facing operation.

    Used as a progress_factory: each phase asking for a bar gets a slice of this one, so the bar runs
    empty to full once, never restarting or going backwards.

    `phases` is the number of phase-sized units the operation expects and sizes the slices; extra phases
    take from what is left, missing ones are filled in at the end. A phase worth several siblings claims
    weight=n units. The bar is painted when the operation starts, before its first phase reports.

    `emit` makes a headless twin for work off the Qt thread, reporting positions instead of moving a bar,
    as Qt widgets may only be touched from their own thread; build it with worker_twin() so it starts
    where the bar is.

    A long operation logs its progress every `heartbeat_seconds`, to tell a slow phase from a hung one.
    The bar keeps the operation's description; only a long step (see set_step()) is named after it.
    """

    # just the time estimate: napari's eta label is everything after the last '|'
    bar_format = '{desc}|{elapsed}<{remaining}'

    # ticks of the whole operation; a phase maps its own steps onto its slice of these
    ticks = 1000

    # long enough that a short operation never logs, short enough to see a long one is alive
    heartbeat_seconds = 30

    # the bar, and a worker's position, shown at most this often: each move is a redraw, or a signal to the Qt thread
    min_update_seconds = 1.0

    # share of the remainder for the last expected phase: only the operation's end fills the bar,
    # and an unexpected extra phase still has room
    last_phase_share = 0.9

    def __init__(self, progress_class=None, desc=None, phases=1, min_duration=0.0, emit=None,
                 emit_step=None, **progress_kwargs):
        from napari.utils import progress

        self.progress_class = progress_class or progress
        self.emit = emit
        self.emit_step = emit_step
        self.desc = desc
        self.step = None
        progress_kwargs.setdefault('bar_format', self.bar_format)
        self.phases = max(int(phases), 1)
        self.phases_left = self.phases
        self.min_duration = max(float(min_duration), 0.0)
        self.progress_kwargs = progress_kwargs
        self._pbar = None
        self._started_at = None
        self._position = 0.0
        self._target = 0.0
        self._moving = False
        self._shown_at = None
        self._heartbeat = None
        self._done = threading.Event()

    def __enter__(self):
        self._started_at = time.monotonic()
        if self.emit is None:
            kwargs = dict(self.progress_kwargs)
            kwargs['total'] = self.ticks
            if self.desc is not None:
                kwargs['desc'] = self.desc
            self._pbar = self.progress_class(**kwargs)
            _paint_now()
        self._start_heartbeat()
        return self

    def __call__(self, total=None, desc=None, weight=1, **_):
        return _ProgressPhase(self, total, desc, weight)

    def worker_twin(self, emit, emit_step=None):
        """A bar-less stand-in for work on another thread, starting where this bar is. Hand its final state
        back with continue_from().
        """
        twin = NapariPhaseProgress(emit=emit, emit_step=emit_step, phases=self.phases)
        twin._position = self._position
        twin._target = self._target
        twin.min_update_seconds = self.min_update_seconds
        twin.last_phase_share = self.last_phase_share
        twin.phases_left = self.phases_left
        return twin

    def continue_from(self, twin):
        """Take over a twin's position and phases used, so later phases do not re-divide used slices."""
        self.phases_left = twin.phases_left
        self._move_to(twin._target, force=True)

    def set_step(self, step):
        """Name the long step the operation is on (a fusion level) in brackets after its description, on the bar and
        in the log."""
        if self.emit is not None:
            if self.emit_step is not None:
                self.emit_step(step)
            return
        self.step = step
        if self._pbar is not None:
            self._pbar.set_description(self.label)

    @property
    def label(self):
        if self.desc and self.step:
            return f'{self.desc} ({self.step})'
        return self.desc or self.step or 'Working'

    def ensure_phases(self, phases):
        """Make room for a nested operation reporting `phases` of its own into this bar, so it does not keep
        re-dividing the same remainder.
        """
        self.phases_left = max(self.phases_left, float(phases))

    # a filled bar is held before closing: one painted frame is not reliably seen over a remote display
    completion_dwell_seconds = 0.4

    def _report_completed(self):
        """Show, and log, that the operation reached 100%, also when reserved phases never reported."""
        if self.emit is not None:
            return
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - (self._started_at or time.monotonic())
        if self.heartbeat_seconds and elapsed >= self.heartbeat_seconds:
            # only after a heartbeat: a short operation logging just 100% says nothing
            so_far = (f'{elapsed / 60:.1f} minutes' if elapsed >= 60 else f'{elapsed:.0f} seconds')
            logging.info(f'{self.label}: 100% ({so_far}){print_memory_usage()}')
        if elapsed >= self.completion_dwell_seconds:
            time.sleep(self.completion_dwell_seconds)

    def _start_heartbeat(self):
        if self.emit is not None or not self.heartbeat_seconds:
            # a twin reports through the one that owns the bar, which does the logging
            return
        self._done.clear()

        def heartbeat():
            while not self._done.wait(self.heartbeat_seconds):
                elapsed = time.monotonic() - (self._started_at or time.monotonic())
                so_far = (f'{elapsed / 60:.1f} minutes' if elapsed >= 60
                          else f'{elapsed:.0f} seconds')
                logging.info(f'{self.label}:'
                             f' {self._position / self.ticks * 100:.0f}%'
                             f' ({so_far} so far){print_memory_usage()}')

        self._heartbeat = threading.Thread(target=heartbeat, daemon=True,
                                           name='muvis-align progress')
        self._heartbeat.start()

    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_value, traceback):
        self._done.set()
        self._heartbeat = None
        if self._pbar is not None:
            if exc_type is None:
                self._move_to(self.ticks, force=True)
                # filling and closing in one pass would read as giving up rather than finishing
                _paint_now()
                self._report_completed()
            self._pbar.close()
            self._pbar = None
        if self.emit is None:
            # reset so a factory outliving its operation reports on a new bar, not a closed one
            # (a twin is never reused)
            self.phases_left = self.phases
            self.step = None
            self._position = 0.0
            self._target = 0.0
            self._shown_at = None
        if self._started_at is not None and self.min_duration > 0:
            # an instant operation would otherwise flash the activity dock open and shut
            wait_s = self.min_duration - (time.monotonic() - self._started_at)
            if wait_s > 0:
                time.sleep(wait_s)
        self._started_at = None
        return False

    @property
    def tqdm_class(self):
        """A tqdm stand-in whose bars are phases of this one, so a third-party library moves this bar
        instead of opening its own.
        """
        owner = self

        class _PhaseTqdm(_ProgressPhase):
            def __init__(self, iterable=None, desc=None, total=None, **kwargs):
                if total is None:
                    try:
                        total = len(iterable)
                    except TypeError:
                        total = None
                super().__init__(owner, total=total, desc=desc)
                self.iterable = iterable
                self._open = False

            def __iter__(self):
                self._start()
                for item in self.iterable:
                    yield item
                    self.update(1)
                self.close()

            def _start(self):
                if not self._open:
                    self.__enter__()
                    self._open = True
                    if self.desc:
                        owner.set_step(self.desc)

            def update(self, n=1):
                self._start()
                super().update(n)

            def set_description(self, desc=None, refresh=True):
                # a library's bar over several steps (fusion's levels) names each as it starts it
                if desc:
                    self.desc = desc
                    if self._open:
                        owner.set_step(desc)

            def close(self):
                if self._open:
                    self._open = False
                    self.__exit__(None, None, None)

            def __getattr__(self, name):
                # a library may touch any of tqdm's wide surface: a no-op beats an AttributeError mid-loop
                return lambda *args, **kwargs: None

        return _PhaseTqdm

    # share of its remaining slice an update of a phase without a step count crosses: moving, never arriving
    undeclared_step_share = 0.25

    def _check_cancelled(self):
        # only a worker twin stops: the Qt side's own phases (building the view) are never left half done
        if self.emit is not None:
            raise_if_cancelled()

    def _begin_phase(self, total, desc=None, weight=1):
        self._check_cancelled()
        remaining = self.ticks - self._position
        weight = max(float(weight), 1.0)
        if self.phases_left > weight:
            span = remaining * weight / self.phases_left
        else:
            # the last expected phase, or one never expected at all, takes most of the remainder
            span = remaining * self.last_phase_share
        self.phases_left = max(self.phases_left - weight, 0)
        return _PhaseSlice(start=self._position, span=span, total=total)

    def _advance_phase(self, phase_slice, n=1):
        self._check_cancelled()
        phase_slice.done += n
        if phase_slice.total:
            fraction = min(phase_slice.done / phase_slice.total, 1.0)
        else:
            # still moves on every update: parked at a fixed fraction it would look hung
            fraction = 1.0 - (1.0 - self.undeclared_step_share) ** phase_slice.done
        self._move_to(phase_slice.start + phase_slice.span * fraction)

    def _end_phase(self, phase_slice):
        # shown at once: a phase's last update may have been held back, and the next phase can be long
        self._move_to(phase_slice.start + phase_slice.span, force=True)

    def set_position(self, position):
        """Move the bar to a position reported by a twin on a worker thread, which already reports at most once a
        second."""
        self._move_to(position, force=True)

    def _move_to(self, position, force=False):
        # never re-entered: a repaint pumps the Qt loop, which can deliver the next position back here and
        # overflow the stack; a move in progress just raises its target
        self._target = min(max(position, self._position, self._target), self.ticks)
        now = time.monotonic()
        if self._moving or (not force and self._shown_at is not None
                            and now - self._shown_at < self.min_update_seconds):
            return
        self._shown_at = now
        self._moving = True
        try:
            while True:
                # the bar counts in whole ticks, so only a move that crosses one shows up
                step = int(self._target) - int(self._position)
                self._position = self._target
                if step <= 0:
                    break
                if self.emit is not None:
                    self.emit(int(self._position))
                elif self._pbar is not None:
                    self._pbar.update(step)
                if self._target <= self._position:
                    break
        finally:
            self._moving = False

def get_section_dict(template, keys=None):
    """Group bilayers fields by section and return normalized dict items."""
    sections = {}
    if keys is None:
        keys = [None]

    for key in keys:
        items = template.get(key, []) if key is not None else template
        for raw_item in items:
            item = BilayersField.model_validate({**raw_item, 'section_key': key})
            section_id = item.section_id or key
            sections.setdefault(section_id, []).append(item)

    return {
        section_id: [item.model_dump() for item in sorted(section_items, key=lambda item: item.cli_order)]
        for section_id, section_items in sections.items()
    }

def adjust_sbemimage_properties(translation, scale, size, filename, sbemimage_config):
    cfg = ConfigParser()
    cfg.read_string(sbemimage_config)
    if bool(cfg['sys'].get('use_microtome')):
        props = cfg['microtome']
    else:
        props = cfg['sem']
    scale_x = float(props.get('stage_scale_factor_x'))
    scale_y = float(props.get('stage_scale_factor_y'))
    rotation_x = float(props.get('stage_rotation_angle_x'))
    rotation_y = float(props.get('stage_rotation_angle_y'))
    rotation_diff = rotation_x - rotation_y
    rot_mat_a = math.cos(rotation_y) / math.cos(rotation_diff)
    rot_mat_b = -math.sin(rotation_y) / math.cos(rotation_diff)
    rot_mat_c = math.sin(rotation_x) / math.cos(rotation_diff)
    rot_mat_d = math.cos(rotation_x) / math.cos(rotation_diff)
    rot_mat_determinant = rot_mat_a * rot_mat_d - rot_mat_b * rot_mat_c

    pixel_size = None
    parts = split_numeric_dict(filename)
    if 't' in parts:
        grids = cfg['grids']
        if 'r' in parts:
            grid_index = json.loads(grids.get('roi_index')).index(int(parts['r']))
        else:
            grid_index = int(parts['g'])
        pixel_size = json.loads(grids.get('pixel_size'))[grid_index] * 1e-3
    else:
        ov = cfg['overviews']
        if 'ov' in parts:
            ov_index = int(parts['ov'])
            pixel_size = json.loads(ov.get('ov_pixel_size'))[ov_index] * 1e-3
        elif '_stubov_' in filename.lower():
            pixel_size = float(ov.get('stub_ov_pixel_size')) * 1e-3

    if pixel_size:
        scale = {'x': pixel_size, 'y': pixel_size}
    else:
        scale = None

    stage_x, stage_y = translation['x'], translation['y']
    stage_x /= scale_x
    stage_y /= scale_y
    dx = ((rot_mat_d * stage_x - rot_mat_b * stage_y) / rot_mat_determinant)
    dy = ((-rot_mat_c * stage_x + rot_mat_a * stage_y) / rot_mat_determinant)
    # convert center to top/left
    physical_size = {dim: size[dim] * scale[dim] for dim in size}
    translation['x'] = dx - physical_size['x'] / 2
    translation['y'] = dy - physical_size['y'] / 2

    return translation, scale

def background_luminance(levels, colors):
    """The luminance channels shown additively at their display `levels` (get_display_level) in RGB `colors` give
    their background, clipped to 1; None if any level is unknown."""
    if not levels or any(level is None for level in levels):
        return None
    return float(min(1.0, sum(level * (0.2126 * color[0] + 0.7152 * color[1] + 0.0722 * color[2])
                              for level, color in zip(levels, colors))))

def contrasting_color(background):
    """A saturated colour, apart from greyscale by its hue, that stands out on a background of `background` luminance
    (0 black to 1 white): dark on a bright one, bright on a dark one, magenta between or when unknown (None).
    Hex: napari reads an RGB tuple as three colours."""

        return '#990066'
    if background is not None and background < 0.4:
        return '#ffd700'
    return '#ff00ff'

def convert_to_um(value, unit):
    """`value` in `unit`, converted to um; an unrecognised unit is left unscaled, and logged.
    Takes both OME abbreviations and spelled-out NGFF unit names.
    """
    if unit is None:
        return value
    factor = um_conversions.get(unit)
    if factor is None:
        factor = um_conversions.get(str(unit).lower())
    if factor is None:
        if str(unit).strip():
            logging.warning(f'Unrecognised physical unit {unit!r}, treating values as um')
        return value
    return value * factor

def create_transform(center, angle, translation=None, matrix_size=3):
    if not center:
        center = np.array([0] * (matrix_size - 1))
    if isinstance(center, dict):
        dims = 'xyz' if matrix_size >= 4 else 'xy'
        center = dict_to_xyz(center, dims=dims, add_zeros=True)
    if len(center) == 2:
        center = np.array(list(center) + [0])
    if angle is None:
        angle = 0
    r = Rotation.from_euler('z', angle, degrees=True)
    t = center - r.apply(center, inverse=True)
    if translation is not None:
        if len(translation) < len(t):
            translation = list(translation) + [0] * (len(t) - len(translation))
        t += translation
    transform = np.eye(matrix_size)
    transform[:3, :3] = np.transpose(r.as_matrix())
    transform[:3, -1] += t
    return transform

def filter_edge_points(points, bounds, filter_factor=0.1, threshold=0.5):
    center = np.array(bounds) / 2
    dist_center = np.abs(points / center - 1)
    position_weights = np.clip((1 - np.max(dist_center, axis=-1)) / filter_factor, 0, 1)
    order_weights = 1 - np.array(range(len(points))) / len(points) / 2
    weights = position_weights * order_weights
    return weights > threshold

One timing line for a threaded per-item phase: wall time against summed per-item CPU time.

Summed per-item wall time inflates with GIL waits, but per-item CPU (time.thread_time) is a floor: wall ~= cpu means CPU/GIL-bound, more workers cannot help; wall >> cpu means waiting (I/O) that more workers can overlap. process_cpu_time (time.process_time over the phase) also shows CPU spent outside the timed items, such as nested pools or other threads.

def format_phase_timing(wall_time, item_times, item_cpu_times, max_workers, process_cpu_time=None,
                        processes=False):
    """One timing line for a threaded per-item phase: wall time against summed per-item CPU time.

    Summed per-item wall time inflates with GIL waits, but per-item CPU (time.thread_time) is a floor:
    wall ~= cpu means CPU/GIL-bound, more workers cannot help; wall >> cpu means waiting (I/O) that more
    workers can overlap. `process_cpu_time` (time.process_time over the phase) also shows CPU spent outside
    the timed items, such as nested pools or other threads.
    """
    total_time = sum(item_times)
    total_cpu = sum(item_cpu_times) if item_cpu_times else 0.0
    summary = (f'with {max_workers} workers, wall {wall_time:.1f}s,'
               f' per-item total {total_time:.1f}s, cpu {total_cpu:.1f}s'
               f' (mean {1000 * total_time / len(item_times):.0f}ms,'
               f' max {1000 * max(item_times):.0f}ms)')
    if process_cpu_time is not None and wall_time > 0:
        summary += (f', process cpu {process_cpu_time:.1f}s'
                    f' ({process_cpu_time / wall_time:.1f} cores)')
        if total_cpu > 0 and process_cpu_time > 2 * total_cpu:
            summary += (f' - only {total_cpu / process_cpu_time:.0%} of the process CPU is this'
                        f' phase: the rest is elsewhere in the process')
    if processes and total_cpu > 0 and wall_time > 0:
        # no shared GIL: the items' cpu against the wall is how many of the workers were busy
        summary += f' - items in worker processes, {total_cpu / wall_time:.1f} of {max_workers} busy'
    elif total_cpu > 0:
        ratio = wall_time / total_cpu
        regime = ('CPU-bound: at the single-thread floor, more workers will not help'
                  if ratio < 1.3 else
                  f'{1 - 1 / ratio:.0%} of wall time is not CPU: more workers can overlap it')
        summary += f' - {regime}'
    return summary

How far a tile grid is turned, in degrees within (-45, 45], or None without neighbours to tell. Only same-sized neighbours at distinct xy count.

def get_grid_angle(positions, sizes):
    """How far a tile grid is turned, in degrees within (-45, 45], or None without neighbours to tell.
    Only same-sized neighbours at distinct xy count.
    """
    pairs, _ = get_pairs(positions, sizes)
    directions = []
    for first, second in pairs:
        vector = [positions[first].get(dim, 0) - positions[second].get(dim, 0) for dim in 'xy']
        is_same_size = all(math.isclose(sizes[first].get(dim, 0), sizes[second].get(dim, 0), rel_tol=0.01)
                           for dim in 'xy')
        if is_same_size and math.hypot(*vector) > 1e-3 * max(sizes[first].values(), default=0):
            directions.append(math.atan2(vector[1], vector[0]))
    if not directions:
        return None
    # four times the angle: rows and columns, either way round, give the same grid direction
    return math.degrees(math.atan2(np.mean(np.sin(4 * np.array(directions))),
                                   np.mean(np.cos(4 * np.array(directions)))) / 4)

def get_metadata_z_scale(metadata):
    """The configured z spacing from a source/extra metadata dict, as a number - or None when it
    is unset, blank, or 'source' (the file's own, already applied by ImageSource.fix_metadata).
    """
    if not isinstance(metadata, dict):
        return None
    scales = metadata.get('scale', {})
    # a list holds one scale per file: the run steps by the finest z, as init_data does by z positions
    values = []
    for scale in (scales if isinstance(scales, list) else [scales]):
        value = scale.get('z') if isinstance(scale, dict) else None
        if value is not None and not check_contains_value(value, 'source'):
            try:
                values.append(float(value))
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                pass
    return min(values, key=abs) if values else None

def get_pairs(positions, sizes):
    """
    Get pairs of orthogonal neighbors from a list of tiles.
    Tiles don't have to be placed on a regular grid.
    """
    pairs = []
    angles = []
    z_positions = [position['z'] for position in positions if 'z' in position]
    ordered_z = sorted(set(z_positions))
    z_index = {z: index for index, z in enumerate(ordered_z)}
    is_mixed_3dstack = len(ordered_z) < len(z_positions)
    for i, j in _get_pairs_candidates(positions, sizes, is_mixed_3dstack, z_index):
        posi, posj = positions[i], positions[j]
        sizei, sizej = sizes[i], sizes[j]
        if is_mixed_3dstack:
            # ignore z value for distance
            distance = math.dist([posi[dim] for dim in 'xy'], [posj[dim] for dim in 'xy'])
            min_distance = max([size[dim] for size in [sizei, sizej] for dim in 'xy'])
            is_same_z = (posi['z'] == posj['z'])
            is_close_z = abs(z_index[posi['z']] - z_index[posj['z']]) <= 1
            if not is_close_z:
                # if not close, discard as pair
                min_distance = 0
            elif not is_same_z:
                # for tiles in different z stack, require greater overlap
                min_distance *= 0.8
        else:
            distance = math.dist(posi.values(), posj.values())
            min_distance = max(list(sizei.values()) + list(sizej.values()))

        if distance < min_distance:
            pairs.append((int(i), int(j)))
            vector = np.array(list(posi.values())) - np.array(list(posj.values()))
            angle = math.degrees(math.atan2(vector[1], vector[0]))
            if distance < min(list(sizei.values()) + list(sizej.values())):
                angle += 90
            while angle < -90:
                angle += 180
            while angle > 90:
                angle -= 180
            angles.append(angle)
    return pairs, angles

def get_process_memory():
    """This process's (resident, peak resident) memory in bytes, or None where the platform
    will not say (psutil is not a dependency).
    """
    resident = peak = None
    try:
        with open('/proc/self/statm') as file:

    except (OSError, ValueError, AttributeError, IndexError):
        pass

        import resource
        # ru_maxrss is kilobytes on Linux but bytes on macOS
        max_rss = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss
        peak = max_rss if sys.platform == 'darwin' else max_rss * 1024
    except (ImportError, AttributeError, OSError, ValueError):
        pass
    if resident is None and peak is None:
        resident, peak = _windows_process_memory()
    if resident is not None and peak is not None:
        # Linux RSS counters are per-CPU approximations read at different moments, so peak can lag
        peak = max(peak, resident)
    return resident, peak

def get_unique_file_labels(filenames: list) -> list:
    file_labels = []

    ntot = len(filenames)
    common_paths = strip_common_path_prefix(filenames)
    parts_dic = get_unique_nums([split_numeric_dict(get_filetitle(filename)) for filename in filenames])
    parts_dic_full = get_unique_nums([split_numeric_dict(filename) for filename in common_paths])
    parts_num_full = get_unique_nums([{index: value for index, value in enumerate(split_numeric(filename))} for filename in common_paths])

    dic_ok = (len(set(['_'.join(parts.values()) for parts in parts_dic])) == ntot)
    full_dic_ok = (len(set(['_'.join(parts.values()) for parts in parts_dic_full])) == ntot)
    full_num_ok = (len(set(['_'.join(parts.values()) for parts in parts_num_full])) == ntot)

    if dic_ok:
        all_parts = parts_dic
    elif full_dic_ok:
        all_parts = parts_dic_full
    elif full_num_ok:
        all_parts = parts_num_full
    else:
        # no digit-based split told them apart - use the path relative to the shared root
        all_parts = [{0: common_path} for common_path in common_paths]

    for parts in all_parts:
        file_label = '_'.join([key + part if isinstance(key, str) else part for key, part in parts.items()])
        file_labels.append(file_label)

    if len(set(file_labels)) < len(file_labels):
        # fallback for duplicate labels
        file_labels = [get_filetitle(filename) for filename in filenames]

    return file_labels

def normalise_rotated_positions(positions0, rotations0, sizes, center, ndims):
    # in [xy(z)]; each source turns about its own centre, as its image is drawn unrotated
    positions = []
    rotations = []
    grid_angle = get_grid_angle(positions0, sizes)
    for position0, size, rotation in zip(positions0, sizes, rotations0):
        if rotation is None and grid_angle is not None:
            rotation = -grid_angle
        angle = -rotation if rotation is not None else None
        transform = create_transform(center=center, angle=angle, matrix_size=ndims + 1)
        half_size = {dim: size.get(dim, 0) / 2 for dim in 'xy'}
        source_center = {dim: position0.get(dim, 0) + half_size[dim] for dim in 'xy'}
        turned_center = apply_transform_dict([source_center], transform, transform_dims='xy')[0]
        positions.append(dict(position0) | {dim: turned_center[dim] - half_size[dim] for dim in 'xy'})
        rotations.append(rotation)
    return positions, rotations

def parse_scale(value, default=1):
    """A downscale setting as get_level_from_scale() takes it: a factor - a number, or a number as the
    text a text field gives ('2') - or a pixel size with its unit ('10um'), kept as text. Blank is
    `default`; other text is an error naming the units a pixel size can have."""
    if value is None or (isinstance(value, str) and not value.strip()):
        return default
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        return value
    try:
        number = float(value)
    except ValueError:
        if pixel_size_to_um(value) is None:
            raise ValueError(f'{value!r} is neither a downscale factor nor a pixel size with a unit'
                             f' ({", ".join(sorted(set(um_conversions)))})') from None
        return value.strip()
    return int(number) if number.is_integer() else number

def pattern_base_dir(pattern):
    """The real directory an input pattern sits in, without wildcard components (os.path.dirname of
    'data/*/*.tiff' is 'data/*'): what a relative output path is relative to."""
    directory = os.path.dirname(pattern)
    while directory and any(char in os.path.basename(directory) for char in '*?['):
        parent = os.path.dirname(directory)
        if parent == directory:
            return ''
        directory = parent
    return directory

def pooled_map(func, count, workers, progress_factory=None, desc=None, weight=1, timing_label=None):
    """[func(index) for index in range(count)], on `workers` threads (one: none), each on the bar as it finishes; with
    timing_label, the phase's timing logged (format_phase_timing). Rolling: a cancel need not wait for every item."""
    results = [None] * count
    times, cpu_times = [], []
    timed = timed_calls(func, times, cpu_times)
    workers = max(1, min(workers, count))
    phase_start, phase_cpu_start = time.time(), time.process_time()
    with progress_phase(progress_factory, total=count, desc=desc, weight=weight) as pbar:
        items = ((index, timed(index)) for index in range(count)) if workers == 1 \
            else rolling_map(timed, range(count), workers)
        for index, result in items:
            results[index] = result
            if pbar is not None:
                pbar.update(1)
    if timing_label and times:
        logging.info(f'{timing_label}: {len(times)} items {format_phase_timing(
            time.time() - phase_start, times, cpu_times, workers, time.process_time() - phase_cpu_start)}')
    return results

def print_hbytes(nbytes: int) -> str:
    exps = ['', 'K', 'M', 'G', 'T', 'P', 'E']
    div = 1024
    exp = 0

    while nbytes > div:
        nbytes /= div
        exp += 1
    if exp < len(exps):
        e = exps[exp]
    else:
        e = f'e{exp * 3}'
    return f'{nbytes:.1f} {e}B'

def print_significants(value: float, significant_digits: int) -> str:
    # fixed-point rather than 'g', which turns 64863 into 6.49e+04: every integer digit is kept

Hand memory the process has freed back to the OS, logging what that recovered.

glibc's per-thread heaps keep freed buffers below anything still in use; malloc_trim() returns them, elsewhere this only collects garbage. generation 1 collects only young objects, enough after one batch, where a full collection scans every live object.

def release_memory(label=None, generation=2):
    """Hand memory the process has freed back to the OS, logging what that recovered.

    glibc's per-thread heaps keep freed buffers below anything still in use; malloc_trim() returns them,
    elsewhere this only collects garbage. `generation` 1 collects only young objects, enough after one
    batch, where a full collection scans every live object.
    """
    gc.collect(generation)
    if not sys.platform.startswith('linux'):
        return
    try:
        import ctypes
        before, _ = get_process_memory()
        ctypes.CDLL('libc.so.6').malloc_trim(0)
        after, _ = get_process_memory()
    except (OSError, AttributeError):
        return
    if label and before is not None and after is not None:
        logging.info(f'{label}: released {print_hbytes(max(before - after, 0))} to the OS,'
                     f' rss {print_hbytes(before)} -> {print_hbytes(after)}')

def retuple(chunks, shape):
    # from ome-zarr-py
    """
    Expand chunks to match shape.

    E.g. if chunks is (64, 64) and shape is (3, 4, 5, 1028, 1028)
    return (3, 4, 5, 64, 64)

    If chunks is an integer, it is applied to all dimensions, to match
    the behaviour of zarr-python.
    """

    if isinstance(chunks, int):
        return tuple([chunks] * len(shape))

    dims_to_add = len(shape) - len(chunks)
    return *shape[:dims_to_add], *chunks

def rolling_map(func, items, workers):
    """(item, func(item)) for each of `items` as it finishes, on `workers` threads (one: in the calling thread). Only
    twice that many are submitted at once, so memory stays bounded and a slow item holds up only its own thread."""
    if workers <= 1:
        for item in items:
            yield item, func(item)
            raise_if_cancelled()
        return
    items = iter(items)
    pending = {}
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(workers) as pool:
        def submit(count):
            for item in itertools.islice(items, count):
                pending[pool.submit(func, item)] = item

        submit(2 * workers)
        try:
            while pending:
                # woken twice a second even with nothing done, so a cancel need not wait for an item
                done, _ = wait(pending, timeout=0.5, return_when=FIRST_COMPLETED)
                for future in done:
                    yield pending.pop(future), future.result()
                raise_if_cancelled()
                submit(len(done))
        finally:
            # on an error or an early stop, leaving the pool would otherwise still run every queued item
            for future in pending:
                future.cancel()

def single_threaded_highs():
    """Run scipy's HiGHS (linprog, as multiview-stitcher's overlap tests use) on the calling thread alone."""
    # HiGHS starts and tears down workers per calling thread, which can deadlock on the Windows loader lock;
    # these problems are tiny
    try:
        from scipy.optimize import _linprog_highs
    except ImportError:
        return
    highs_wrapper = getattr(_linprog_highs, '_highs_wrapper', None)
    if highs_wrapper is None or getattr(highs_wrapper, '_muvis_single_threaded', False):
        return

    def single_threaded(*args):
        *arrays, options = args
        return highs_wrapper(*arrays, dict(options, threads=1))

    single_threaded._muvis_single_threaded = True
    _linprog_highs._highs_wrapper = single_threaded

def timed_calls(func, times, cpu_times):
    """`func`, appending each call's wall and thread CPU time to `times` and `cpu_times` (for
    format_phase_timing()). Keeps func's signature for callers that inspect it.
    """
    @functools.wraps(func)
    def timed(*args, **kwargs):
        start, cpu_start = time.perf_counter(), time.thread_time()
        try:
            return func(*args, **kwargs)
        finally:
            times.append(time.perf_counter() - start)
            cpu_times.append(time.thread_time() - cpu_start)
    return timed

def apply_windows_atomic_write_retry():
    """Install the retry. Idempotent, and a no-op where it does not apply."""
    global _applied
    if _applied or os.name != 'nt':
        return False

    try:
        import zarr.storage._local as zarr_local
    except ImportError:
        return False
    original = getattr(zarr_local, '_atomic_write', None)
    safe_move = getattr(zarr_local, '_safe_move', None)
    if original is None or safe_move is None:
        # zarr's internals have moved - leave them alone rather than guess
        return False

    @contextlib.contextmanager
    def _atomic_write_with_retry(path, mode, exclusive=False):
        path = Path(path)
        tmp_path = path.with_suffix(f'.{uuid.uuid4().hex}.partial')
        # cleanup on failure only, as the original: on success the temp file has been renamed away
        try:
            with tmp_path.open(mode) as file:
                yield file
            delay, waited, attempts = _FIRST_DELAY_SECONDS, 0.0, 0
            while True:
                try:
                    if exclusive:
                        safe_move(tmp_path, path)
                    else:
                        tmp_path.replace(path)
                    break
                except PermissionError:
                    if waited >= _MAX_WAIT_SECONDS:
                        # a hold this long is not the transient one this exists for
                        raise
                    time.sleep(delay)
                    waited += delay
                    attempts += 1
                    delay = min(delay * 2, 0.2)
            if attempts:
                logging.debug(f'{path.name}: atomic write retried {attempts}x'
                              f' ({waited:.2f}s) - destination was briefly held open')
        except Exception:
            tmp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            raise

    zarr_local._atomic_write = _atomic_write_with_retry
    _applied = True
    return True

docs.title: Technical overview
docs.text: muvis-align is an image registration package for aligning 2D and 3D images. The package is implemented as a napari plugin, notebooks using the package classes, and a command line interface (CLI) for batch processing. The napari plugin can also be run as a container on a local machine or on a cloud platform via an interactive web interface.

docs.title: muvis-align practices demonstrated in the source code
docs.text:
Repository: https://github.com/ccp-volume-em/muvis-align

muvis-align demonstrates practical patterns for scalable, reproducible image registration workflows across a napari plugin, notebooks, CLI execution, batch/HPC use, and containerized interactive access.

docs.title: Next Generation File Formats (NGFF)
docs.text:
muvis-align uses OME-Zarr / NGFF as a primary output format.

OME-Zarr / NGFF writing is delegated to to_multiscales and to_ngff_zarr from ngff-zarr, including multiscale pyramid generation.

Source: src/muvis_align/image/ome_zarr_helper.py

from ngff_zarr import to_ngff_image, to_multiscales, to_ngff_zarr


def save_ome_image(data, path, dim_order, pixel_size, channels, translation, rotation,
                   pyramid_downsample=None, compression=None, ome_version=default_ome_zarr_version):

    storage_options = {}
    compressor, compression_filters = create_compression_filter(compression)
    if compressor is not None:
        storage_options['compressor'] = compressor
    if compression_filters is not None:
        storage_options['filters'] = compression_filters

    axes_units = {dim: 'micrometer' for dim in dim_order if dim in 'xyz'}
    image = to_ngff_image(data, dims=dim_order, scale=pixel_size, translation=translation, axes_units=axes_units)
    multiscales = to_multiscales(image, scale_factors=pyramid_downsample, chunks=create_chunk_dict(default_chunk_size, dim_order))
    ...
    to_ngff_zarr(path, multiscales, chunks_per_shard=chunks_per_shard, version=ome_version, **storage_options)

    return multiscales.metadata

docs.title: Handling larger-than-memory data
docs.text:
The code uses Dask-backed image sources for lazy loading and chunked processing.

Source: src/muvis_align/image/source_helper.py

def create_image_source(filename, source_metadata=None, file_label=None, index=None, transform_key=None):
    kwargs = {'file_label': file_label, 'index': index}
    if transform_key is not None:
        kwargs['transform_key'] = transform_key
    ext = os.path.splitext(filename)[1].lstrip('.').lower()
    if ext.startswith('tif'):
        source = TiffImageSource(filename, source_metadata, **kwargs)
    elif '.zar' in filename.lower():
        source = ZarrImageSource(filename, source_metadata, **kwargs)
    else:
        if ext:
            raise ValueError(f'Unsupported file type: {ext}')
        else:
            raise ValueError(f'Unsupported: {filename}')
    return source

TIFF files are read lazily through tifffile's Zarr store (aszarr), each pyramid level wrapped as a Dask array, avoiding immediate full-volume loading.

Source: src/muvis_align/image/ome_tiff_helper.py

with tifffile.TiffFile(filename) as tif:
    series = tif.series[0]
    axes = series.axes
    # multiscales=True: a group even for one level, levels ordered finest first
    group = zarr.open_group(store=tif.aszarr(series=0, multiscales=True), mode='r')
    attributes = group.attrs.get('ome', group.attrs)
    datasets = attributes['multiscales'][0]['datasets']
    arrays = []
    for dataset in datasets:
        array = group[dataset['path']]
        ...
for level, array in enumerate(arrays):
    # meta given, so dask does not probe the dtype with a read
    data = da.from_array(array, chunks=array.chunks, meta=np.empty((0,) * array.ndim, dtype=array.dtype),
                         name='tiff-' + tokenize(filename, stat.st_size, stat.st_mtime_ns, level))
    datas.append(data)

OME-Zarr metadata is read from the store's consolidated metadata (falling back to ngff-zarr's parser), and each multiscale level is opened directly as a Dask array.

Source: src/muvis_align/image/ZarrImageSource.py

def init_metadata(self):
    # metadata only, off consolidated metadata: the arrays wait for first access to self.data
    metadata = read_ome_zarr_source_metadata(self.filename)

    self.dimension_order = metadata['dimension_order']
    self.shapes = metadata['shapes']
    self.shape = self.shapes[0]
    self.dtype = metadata['dtype']
    ...

def _load_data(self):
    ...
    datas = []
    for path, sim_shape in zip(self._level_paths, self.shapes):
        data = da.from_zarr(self.filename, component=path)
        if tuple(data.shape) != tuple(sim_shape):
            data = data.reshape(sim_shape)
        datas.append(data)
    self._data = datas

Fusion writes directly to OME-Zarr, level by level and block by block, rather than creating a full fused array in memory first.

Source: src/muvis_align/MVSRegistration.py, src/muvis_align/fusion_blocks.py

with dask.config.set(scheduler='threads'), warnings.catch_warnings():
    if saving_zarr:
        levels = export_levels(source_spacings, output_stack_properties, scaled_dims, native=is_native)
        fused_image = fuse_levels_to_ome_zarr(
            msims, levels, output_filename, transform_key, output_stack_properties, output_chunksize,
            fusion_func=fuse_func, zarr_options=zarr_options,
            batch_options=self._fusion_batch_options(saving_zarr, max_workers=workers),
            ranks=source_spacings if is_native else None, average_levels=not is_native,
            level_weights=level_bytes)
    else:
        fused_image = fusion.fuse(msims, fusion_func=fuse_func, transform_key=transform_key,
                                  output_stack_properties=output_stack_properties,
                                  output_chunksize=output_chunksize)

docs.title: FAIR implementation
docs.text:
Rather than only documenting FAIR principles, muvis-align implements concrete FAIR-supporting mechanisms:

  • project template defined as workflow schema in Bilayers format
  • structured parameters in YAML
  • OME-Zarr / OME-TIFF image outputs
  • RO-Crate generation
  • persistent mappings and metrics files
  • napari and CLI interfaces
  • container metadata for reproducible execution

docs.title: Declarative UI definition based on workflow schema
docs.text:
Source: src/muvis_align/ui/project_template.yaml

The project_template.yaml file is written in the Bilayers format and serves as the declarative description of the muvis-align workflow. The file is used to dynamically generate the magicgui-based napari user interface, allowing workflow parameters, input definitions, and processing options to be defined in a structured configuration file rather than being hard-coded in the application. This approach simplifies interface maintenance, improves reproducibility, and enables the same workflow definition to be reused across the napari plugin, command-line execution, and containerized deployments. Bilayers schemas are represented as a Pydantic model, which adds typed validation and structured serialization for this workflow definition layer.

Source: src/muvis_align/ui/bilayers_util.py

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, field_validator


class BilayersField(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='allow')

    name: str
    type: str
    label: str | None = None
    default: Any = None
    description: str | None = None
    section_id: str | None = None
    section_key: str | None = None
    cli_order: int = 0
    options: list[BilayersOption] | None = None
    file_count: str | None = None
    output_dir_set: bool = False

    @field_validator('type', mode='before')
    @classmethod
    def _normalize_type(cls, value):
        return str(value).lower()

    @field_validator('cli_order', mode='before')
    @classmethod
    def _normalize_cli_order(cls, value):
        if value is None or value == '':
            return 0
        return int(value)


def get_section_dict(template, keys=None):
    sections = {}
    if keys is None:
        keys = [None]

    for key in keys:
        items = template.get(key, []) if key is not None else template
        for raw_item in items:
            item = BilayersField.model_validate({**raw_item, 'section_key': key})
            section_id = item.section_id or key
            sections.setdefault(section_id, []).append(item)

    return {
        section_id: [item.model_dump() for item in sorted(section_items, key=lambda item: item.cli_order)]
        for section_id, section_items in sections.items()
    }

The package creates a Workflow Run RO-Crate for each run, recording the project parameters, source images and results.

Source: src/muvis_align/file/rocrate_utils.py

def create_workflow_run_crate(dest_path, params_path, params, source_paths, result_paths,
                              start_time=None, end_time=None):
    crate = ROCrate()
    root = crate.root_dataset
    root['name'] = f'muvis-align run: {get_filetitle(os.path.normpath(dest_path))}'
    for profile_id, profile_name in WORKFLOW_RUN_PROFILES.items():
        profile = crate.add(ContextEntity(crate, profile_id, {'@type': ['CreativeWork', 'Profile'],
                                                              'name': profile_name, 'version': '0.5'}))
        root.append_to('conformsTo', profile)

    workflow_entity = add_workflow(crate)
    parameters = add_formal_parameters(crate, workflow_entity)
    ...
    action_entity = crate.add_action(workflow_entity, identifier='#run-001', object=objects, result=results,
                                     properties=action_properties)
    root.append_to('mentions', action_entity)

    crate.write(dest_path)
    return crate

OME-Zarr outputs receive a Zarr-specific RO-Crate, recording the sources, acquisition, registration metrics and the fusion step.

Source: src/muvis_align/file/rocrate_utils.py

def create_zarr_ro_crate(dest_path, sources=None, source_paths=(), metrics=None):
    crate = ZarrCrate()
    # the crate is written as the fusion ends
    fusion_time = to_iso_datetime(datetime.now())
    properties = {'name': get_filetitle(dest_path),
                  'description': f'OME-Zarr image fused by muvis-align from {len(source_paths)} sources',
                  'datePublished': fusion_time,
                  'encodingFormat': ZARR_ENCODING_FORMAT}
    dataset_entity = crate.add_dataset(dest_path='.', properties=properties)
    source_entities = [crate.add(ContextEntity(crate, to_crate_path(source_path, dest_path), {
        '@type': 'Dataset' if os.path.isdir(source_path) else 'File'})) for source_path in source_paths]
    if source_entities:
        dataset_entity['isBasedOn'] = source_entities
    if sources:
        add_data_capture(crate, dataset_entity, sources, source_entities)
    ...
    fusion_properties = {'@type': 'CreateAction', 'name': 'Fusion to OME-Zarr', 'endTime': fusion_time,
                         'instrument': add_software(crate), 'result': dataset_entity}
    if source_entities:
        fusion_properties['object'] = source_entities
    fusion_entity = crate.add(ContextEntity(crate, '#fusion-001', fusion_properties))
    dataset_entity.append_to('mentions', fusion_entity)
    crate.write(dest_path)
    return crate

docs.title: Persistent metadata
docs.text: Input metadata is read from OME-TIFF or OME-Zarr and converted into physical units, positions, rotations, channels, scales, and transforms.

docs.title: Interoperable NGFF RFC 6 transforms
docs.text:
Registration transforms are written in the OME-NGFF RFC 6 coordinate-transform format rather than as application-specific matrix arrays. Each affine identifies its image path and names its input (source_metadata) and output (registered) coordinate systems. Using the ome-zarr-models v0.6 model for both serialization and validation makes the saved transforms portable to other tools that implement the NGFF coordinate-system and transformation model.

Source: src/muvis_align/file/transforms.py

def metadata_models(path, transform, source_key='source_metadata', transform_key='registered'):
    affine = Affine(
        path=path,
        affine=transform,
        input=CoordinateSystemIdentifier(name=source_key),
        output=CoordinateSystemIdentifier(name=transform_key),
    )
    return affine.model_dump(exclude_none=True, exclude_defaults=True, exclude_unset=True)


def read_transforms(filename):
    transforms = import_json(filename)
    return {label: Affine.model_validate(transform).affine for label, transform in transforms.items()}

Source: src/muvis_align/image/ome_zarr_util.py

multiscale = multiscales[0]
file_dims = tuple(axis['name'] for axis in multiscale.get('axes', []))

file_shapes, scales, dtypes = [], [], set()
translation = {}
for index, dataset in enumerate(multiscale.get('datasets', [])):
    node = nodes.get(dataset.get('path'))
    transforms = dataset.get('coordinateTransformations', [])
    scale_values = next((transform['scale'] for transform in transforms
                         if transform.get('type') == 'scale'), None)
    shape = node.get('shape')
    file_shapes.append(tuple(shape))
    scales.append(dict(zip(file_dims, scale_values)))
    if index == 0:
        translation_values = next((transform['translation'] for transform in transforms
                                   if transform.get('type') == 'translation'), None)
        if translation_values is not None:
            translation = dict(zip(file_dims, translation_values))

The workflow builds an MSIM object for each source and performs pairwise/global registration on these multiscale spatial images.

Source: src/muvis_align/MVSRegistration.py

def build_msim(index):
    return build_source_msim(self.sources[index], self._msim_output_order, self.positions[index],
                             self._msim_transforms[index], self.source_transform_key,
                             z_scale=self._msim_z_scale, from_level=from_levels[index] if from_levels else 0,
                             ends_only=ends_only)

msims = pooled_map(build_msim, len(self.sources), default_msim_build_workers, progress_factory,
                   desc='Building sources', weight=weight,
                   timing_label='Build msims' if self.logging_time else None)
...
results = self.register_global(self.pair_msims, register_indices=register_indices, params=params)

The parsed OME metadata (axes, units, voxel scale, translations/positions, channels, and coordinate transforms) is preserved in this xarray-based MSIM (multiscale-spatial-image) representation, where image data remains in labeled dimensions and spatial context is stored as coordinates/attributes. This metadata is propagated through image operations, updated during pairwise/global registration, and carried into fusion/export (for example, OME-Zarr) to preserve physical-space interpretation and multiscale provenance.

The CLI runs the pipeline from a YAML parameter file.

Source: run.py

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=f'muvis-align')
parser.add_argument('params',
                    help='The parameters file',
                    default='resources/params.yml')

args = parser.parse_args()
print(f'Parameters file: {args.params}')
with open(args.params, 'r', encoding='utf8') as file:
    params = yaml.safe_load(file)

pipeline = Pipeline(params, params_path=args.params)
pipeline.run()

docs.title: Performance metrics
docs.text: The project calculates registration metrics such as NCC, SSIM, normalized mutual information, MSE-derived score, match rate, and distance-based feature metrics.

docs.title: Registration quality metrics
docs.text:
muvis-align computes several complementary image similarity metrics to evaluate registration quality. Each metric captures a different aspect of alignment quality, making it useful to evaluate multiple metrics together rather than relying on a single score.

Metric Full name Measures Typical range NCC Normalized Cross-Correlation Intensity correlation between images -1 to 1 SSIM Structural Similarity Index Measure Similarity of local image structures 0 to 1 ONMI Overlapping Normalized Mutual Information Shared information between overlapping image regions 0 to 1+

The metrics are implemented in metrics.py:

all_metric_funcs = {
    'ncc': multiview_stitcher.metrics.normalized_cross_correlation,
    'ssim': lambda im1, im2: structural_similarity(
        np.nan_to_num(im1),
        np.nan_to_num(im2),
        data_range=data_range),
    'onmi': lambda im1, im2:
        normalized_mutual_information(
            np.nan_to_num(im1),
            np.nan_to_num(im2)) - 1,
    'mse': lambda im1, im2:
        1 / mean_squared_error(im1, im2),
}

Source: src/muvis_align/metrics.py

docs.title: NCC — Normalized Cross-Correlation
docs.text:
NCC measures the correlation of image intensities between two images. It is particularly useful when corresponding structures have similar brightness values.

  • NCC = 1 indicates perfect correlation.
  • NCC = 0 indicates no correlation.
  • Negative values indicate inverse correlation.

NCC is computationally efficient and widely used for rigid image registration, although it can be sensitive to intensity variations between acquisitions.

docs.title: SSIM — Structural Similarity Index Measure
docs.text:
SSIM evaluates the similarity of local image structure by comparing:

  • intensity
  • contrast
  • local texture

Unlike pixel-wise metrics, SSIM is sensitive to structural preservation and is therefore useful for assessing whether biological features remain aligned after registration.

  • SSIM = 1 indicates identical structure.
  • Values close to zero indicate poor structural agreement.

SSIM is often more representative of perceived image quality than correlation-based metrics.

docs.title: ONMI — Overlapping Normalized Mutual Information
docs.text:
ONMI measures the amount of shared information between overlapping image regions.

Mutual information is particularly valuable when images originate from different modalities, channels, or acquisition conditions because it does not assume similar intensity values.

Higher ONMI values indicate that:

  • corresponding image regions contain similar information,
  • overlapping structures are well aligned,
  • registration improves the statistical dependence between views.

Because ONMI is based on image information content rather than intensity similarity, it is often more robust for multimodal registration problems.

Using NCC, SSIM, and ONMI together provides complementary measures of registration quality:

  • NCC evaluates intensity agreement.
  • SSIM evaluates structural similarity.
  • ONMI evaluates shared image information.

This combination gives a more robust assessment of registration performance than any single metric alone.

docs.title: Storing data for resumable workflows
docs.text:
muvis-align stores intermediate registration state in mapping and metrics files, allowing workflows to continue from pairwise registration, global registration, or fused output.

Source: src/muvis_align/constants.py

default_pair_mappings_name = 'pair_mappings.json'
default_mappings_name = 'mappings.json'
metrics_name = 'metrics.json'
default_mappings_tabular_name = 'mappings.csv'

The registration state machine tracks progress through the workflow.

Source: src/muvis_align/MVSRegistration.py

class RegState(Enum):
    UNINIT = auto()
    INIT = auto()
    SIMS_INIT = auto()
    PAIRS_REG = auto()
    GLOBAL_REG = auto()
    FUSED = auto()

Existing output files are detected before re-running expensive steps.

Source: src/muvis_align/MVSRegistration.py

def check_progress(self, output_filename, output_format):
    pair_mappings_filename = self.output + self.output_params.get('pair_mappings', default_pair_mappings_name)
    mappings_filename = self.output + self.output_params.get('mappings', default_mappings_name)
    if self.output_exists(output_filename, output_format):
        self.state = RegState.FUSED
    elif os.path.exists(mappings_filename):
        self.state = RegState.GLOBAL_REG
    elif os.path.exists(pair_mappings_filename):
        self.state = RegState.PAIRS_REG

Pair mappings, final mappings, and metrics are saved separately.

Source: src/muvis_align/MVSRegistration.py

def register(self, register_msims=None, register_indices=None, params=None):
    pair_results = self.register_pairs(register_msims=register_msims, register_indices=register_indices, params=params)
    self.save_pair_results(pair_results['pair_mappings'], metrics=pair_results['metrics'])
    results = self.register_global(self.pair_msims, register_indices=register_indices, params=params)
    self.save_group_pair_mappings()
    self.save_mappings(results['mappings'])
    self.save_metrics(results['metrics'])
    return results

docs.title: Restoring registered transforms from intermediate output
docs.text:
Registered alignment transforms are persisted as JSON intermediate outputs (pair_mappings.json and mappings.json) and reloaded on later runs when these files already exist.

Source: src/muvis_align/MVSRegistration.py

def check_progress(self, output_filename, output_format):
    pair_mappings_filename = self.output + self.output_params.get('pair_mappings', default_pair_mappings_name)
    mappings_filename = self.output + self.output_params.get('mappings', default_mappings_name)
    if self.output_exists(output_filename, output_format):
        self.state = RegState.FUSED
    elif os.path.exists(mappings_filename):
        self.state = RegState.GLOBAL_REG
    elif os.path.exists(pair_mappings_filename):
        self.state = RegState.PAIRS_REG

When progress indicates pairwise/global registration already exists, init_progress loads saved mappings and reapplies transforms to the MSIMs instead of recomputing registration.

Source: src/muvis_align/MVSRegistration.py

if self.is_global_registered():
    mappings = read_transforms(mappings_filename)
    ...
    self.mappings = {}
    for index, filename in enumerate(self.filenames):
        self.mappings[index] = xaffine_from_matrix(find_file_dict_item(mappings, filename))
    if self._msims is not None:
        self._apply_mappings(self._msims)

JSON persistence/reload is handled by shared utilities:

Source: src/muvis_align/util.py

def import_json(filename):
    with open(filename, encoding='utf8') as file:
        data = json.load(file)
    return data


def export_json(filename, data):
    with open(filename, 'w', encoding='utf8') as file:
        json.dump(data, file, indent=4)

docs.title: Interactive interface with Xpra container
docs.text:
The Dockerfile defines a standard napari container and a second Xpra-enabled image for browser-based interactive use.

Source: Dockerfile. docker-build-push.sh [version] builds the Xpra image and pushes it to quay.io/ccp-volume-em/muvis-align-xpra, tagged with the version (by default the latest GitHub release) and latest; it needs docker login quay.io.

FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm AS muvis-align
...
COPY requirements.txt .

RUN python -m pip install --upgrade pip
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
RUN pip install napari[all]
RUN pip install napari-ome-zarr

COPY run.py .
COPY pyproject.toml .
COPY src/ src/

RUN --mount=type=bind,source=.git,target=/app/.git \
    pip install .

ENTRYPOINT ["python3", "-m", "napari", "--plugin", "muvis-align"]

The Xpra stage installs Xpra and launches napari through a browser-accessible session.

Source: Dockerfile

FROM muvis-align AS muvis-align-xpra
...
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -yqq \

    --html=on \
    ...
    --resize-display=yes \
    --start-child="$XPRA_START" \
    --exit-with-children="$XPRA_EXIT_WITH_CHILDREN" \
    --exit-with-client="$XPRA_EXIT_WITH_CLIENT" \

    --pulseaudio=no \

docs.title: On a Slurm cluster
docs.text: On the cluster, Apptainer runs the Xpra image from a sandbox that xpra-pull.sh builds, and xpra-run.sh starts it in a Slurm job. Both run from a folder holding the scripts, which also holds the container.

docs.title: From your own machine
docs.text:
xpra-connect.sh does all of this from your own machine with one command:

bash xpra-connect.sh <user>@<login node> [folder on the cluster, default: muvis-align] [--pull]

On Windows, run it in Git Bash, or from PowerShell as .\xpra-connect.sh <user>@<login node>, which opens it in a Git Bash window that waits for Enter before closing. bash in PowerShell is WSL's; there it uses Windows' own ssh when WSL's cannot sign in.

It copies xpra-run.sh and xpra-pull.sh into the folder on the cluster (replacing what is there), builds the container first if there is none yet (or with --pull), submits the job, tunnels to the compute node the job starts on, and opens napari in your browser, already logged in. Closing napari ends the job; Ctrl-C closes the connection and offers to cancel the job. MUVIS_PARTITION, MUVIS_DATA_DIR and MUVIS_CONTAINER_DIR set locally are passed on to the cluster. With an SSH key on the login node you are not asked for a password.

docs.title: Step by step, on the cluster
docs.text:
With the two scripts in a folder on the cluster (e.g. a clone of this repository), on the login node:

bash xpra-pull.sh     # once, and to update: builds the container sandbox beside the scripts
bash xpra-run.sh      # submits the job, waits for it to start and prints how to connect

Then follow the printed steps on your own machine: open the ssh -N -L ... tunnel it shows, open http://localhost:9876/ in your browser and log in with the user name and password it shows. sbatch xpra-run.sh works too; the steps are then in muvis-align-<job id>.log and the password in ~/.xpra/job-<job id>/passwd. The partition and data directory can be set with the same MUVIS_* variables; the job's resources are the #SBATCH lines at the top of xpra-run.sh. Its memory (--mem) is passed into the container, where fusion's blocks share a quarter of it and napari sizes its image cache against it: the script's 64G is enough for a 34,000-tile project.

sbatch apptainer-check.sh checks whether the compute nodes can run the image's SIF file directly, or unpack it on every start, in which case the sandbox xpra-pull.sh builds is the faster choice; its verdict is at the end of muvis-align-apptainer-check-<job id>.log.
